newsitem.title: USA: DuPont contractor awarded $7.7 mln damages.
newsitem.headline: DuPont contractor awarded $7.7 mln damages.

text.p: A Delaware jury on Tuesday awarded $3.5 million in punitive damages to a contractor that charged DuPont Co with breach of agreement and fraudulent misrepresentation, adding to $4.2 million in compensatory damages awarded last week.
The award followed the jury's finding that DuPont acted willfully when after two years it ended a purported long-term agreement made in 1987 with NSN International Industries NV.

NSN and Rank Enterprises Inc supplied DuPont with advanced technology and design for armor systems for $118,000 a month. DuPont used the technology in a failed bid for a multi-million-dollar U.S. defense contract for upgrading armor systems to compete with those of the former Soviet Union.
DuPont estimated the market potential for upgrading U.S. ground armored vehicles to be $731 million, court papers say.
DuPont attorney David Burt told Reuters the company would appeal.
"We feel there was no breach of contract....DuPont never made a dime in the armor business," Burt said.

"We wound up making a multi- million-dollar investment that didn't pay off. Our product wound up being something the government did not want to buy....Continued payments were not good business sense considering the market at the time," he said.

DuPont also alleged that NSN and Rank did not own the technology but were left in its possession when the owner, a Hare Krishna spiritual leader named Jayatirtha, was murdered. Jayatirtha allegedly gave the technology, stored on computer disks, to Amnon Reshef, a Rank executive and retired Israeli general.
On Tuesday the jury returned after deliberating for about a half hour with an award of $3.5 million in punitive damages to add to last week's award of $4.2 million in compensatory damages.
NSN is based in the Netherland Antilles. Rank, based in Wilmington, Delaware, was also a plaintiff, but it was awarded no damages.
